::: {#sol-two-features-ten-digits}

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
def nearest_mean_accuracy(features, labels):
    """Share of images whose nearest digit average is their own digit."""
    means = np.array([features[labels == k].mean(axis=0) for k in range(10)])
    # Squared distance from every image (rows) to every digit's average (columns).
    distances = ((features[:, None, :] - means[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=2)
    return np.mean(distances.argmin(axis=1) == labels)

hand_features = np.column_stack([center_ink, left_ink])
acc_hand = nearest_mean_accuracy(hand_features, labels)
acc_guess = np.bincount(labels).max() / len(labels)
print(round(acc_hand, 3), round(acc_guess, 3))
```

The two [features](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/course-overview.html#def-feature) get `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$acc_hand)`% of the images right.
Guessing the most common digit gets `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$acc_guess)`% right,
so the features carry real information,
but more than half of the images are still misread.
These shares are measured on the same images the digit averages were computed from,
so they are training accuracies, and new images would likely do a little worse.
Doing better this way means designing more features,
and features designed for digits do not carry over to faces, speech or text.

:::
